focus: Angle 1 inventory: commands tree vs bridge inventory in both directions, per-runtime enablement, and the one runnable-string path in render.ts
noveltyJustification: All 9 findings are net-new to this lineage: no prior packet evidence existed, and each comes from a first read of the commands tree, the generated bridge inventory, allow-list.json or render.ts.
keyQuestions: Which of the 45 commands in .skilled/commands have an active advisor bridge, which bridges point at retired or unmatched names, and what would one drift-proof inventory require?
Why do plain planning and research prompts return zero recommendations, and what do the no-slash penalty and the mutating-command gate cost in recall versus what they buy in precision?
What must the advisor_recommend output contract carry (kind, runnable, brief wording, token budget) for a model to act on a surfaced command instead of a raw bridge id?
Which commands are safe to start without asking, which need a question first, and where should that run-or-ask policy live?
Can a model start a slash command by itself on Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, Cursor, Devin and DSH, and what fallback exists where it cannot?
Which mechanism actually brings a plain-chat request onto the command workflow on every runtime: advisor brief, AGENTS.md gate, hook, skill-to-command pointer, or runner refusal?
Which command workflows never load the mode SKILL.md their metadata names, and should a skill recommendation imply its command?
Which benchmark rows and metrics separate a missed command from a wrongly started one?

What prior art exists for routing free text to a packaged workflow, and which failure modes (over-trigger, command/skill ambiguity, child sessions starting commands, loops, brief budget) must a design guard against?
ruledOut: Counting commands with a recursive find over .skilled/commands: the doctor fixture tree doubles the count to 90
Treating the 62 bridge entries as 62 commands: entries over-count doctor subcommands and under-count five shipped commands

graphEvents.label: Which commands have an active bridge and what does a drift-proof inventory need
Only doctor bridge ids render as runnable commands

label: .skilled/commands holds exactly 45 command markdown files (13 create, 3 deep, 3 design, 17 doctor, 1 local-skilled-alignment, 1 prompt, 7 speckit); a recursive walk reports 90 because doctor/scripts/tests/fixtures contains fixture command folders, so any inventory count must exclude fixture paths.
The bridge inventory is a sum of three sources: 19 command-metadata entries from three hubs, 8 allow-list entries, 35 doctor routes = 62 entries covering 43 distinct command strings.
Only system-deep-loop, sk-design and sk-doc declare command-metadata.json, so most command groups reach the inventory only through hand-maintained allow-list entries or doctor routes.

Five shipped commands have no bridge entry under their own command string: /local-skilled-alignment, /prompt:improve, /speckit:handoff, /speckit:save, /speckit:search; /prompt:improve is reachable only through a legacy /prompt id whose allow-list reason admits the mismatch.
Three bridge commands have no command file: /memory:save (two ids), /prompt and the deprecated /spec_kit, so the inventory carries dead endpoints.

The TypeScript scorer enables only 40 of 62 entries, leaving 22 commands with no TS-enabled bridge, including /speckit:plan, /speckit:implement, /speckit:complete, /speckit:resume, /deep:research, /deep:review, all three /design:* commands and 11 /create:* commands; those are exactly the groups behind the spec's measured zero-recommendation prompts.

Ten command strings carry multiple bridge ids, all doctor routes (e.g. /doctor:skill-advisor has six), so bridge ids are finer-grained than commands and a per-id recommendation surface cannot become a per-command contract without a grouping key.

render.ts has exactly one runnable-string path and it is doctor-only: recommendationLabel() returns doctorCommandString() for command-doctor-* ids from a 35-entry hand-generated map and the raw sanitized id for everything else.

The recommendation payload already carries an internal kind field with a command variant, but no inventory source marks an entry as a command kind, so the kind is a rendering-time widening of caller input rather than declared metadata.
